name_en: Vertically Opposite Angles and Angles on a Straight Line
name_si: ප්‍රතිමුඛ කෝණ සහ සරල රේඛාවක් මත බද්ධ කෝණ
formal_statement: When two straight lines intersect, the vertically opposite angles formed are equal, and adjacent angles on a straight line sum to 180 degrees.
required_conditions: Lines intersecting at the vertex must be continuous straight lines.
Angles on a straight line must share a common straight base line.

bugs.description: Equating angles on a straight line to 360 degrees instead of 180 degrees.
Treating non-collinear rays as forming vertically opposite angles.
Writing the final angle value without stating the straight-line or vertically opposite angle justification.
Correctly applying both supplementary straight-line sum (180 degrees) and vertically opposite angle equality.

name_en: Adjacent Angles on a Straight Line
name_si: සරල රේඛාවක් මත පිහිටි බද්ධ කෝණ
formal_statement: The sum of adjacent angles formed on one side of a straight line at a given point is equal to 180 degrees (two right angles).
required_conditions: All rays must originate from a common point on a single straight line.
All rays must lie on the same side of the straight line.

bugs.description: Setting the sum of angles on one side of a straight line to 360 degrees or 90 degrees.
Applying the angle-at-a-point property (360 degrees) to angles on a half-plane.
Omitting the algebraic factorization step 2(x + y) = 180 degrees before concluding x + y = 90 degrees.
Summing all adjacent angles to 180 degrees and simplifying accurately.

name_en: Interior Angle Sum of a Triangle
topic: Angle Sum of a Triangle and Vertically Opposite Angles
formal_statement: The sum of the three interior angles of any triangle is 180 degrees.
required_conditions: The figure must be a closed three-sided polygon (triangle).
All three angles must be interior angles of the same triangle.

bugs.description: Using the exterior intersection angle (120 degrees) directly as the interior vertex angle without subtracting from 180 degrees.
Assuming both meeting triangles are isosceles or congruent without given conditions.
Jumping directly to x = 30 degrees without showing how the third interior angle (60 degrees) was obtained.
Finding the 60 degree interior angle via straight-line supplement and summing interior angles to 180 degrees.

name_en: Exterior Angle of a Triangle Theorem
formal_statement: If one side of a triangle is produced, the exterior angle so formed is equal to the sum of the two interior opposite angles.
required_conditions: One side of the triangle must be extended as a straight line beyond the vertex.
The two summed angles must be the interior opposite angles (excluding the adjacent interior angle).

bugs.description: Subtracting the interior opposite angles (3x - 2x = 150) or adding the adjacent interior angle.
Setting 3x + 2x = 180 degrees by confusing the exterior angle property with the interior angle sum theorem.
In multi-triangle figures, skipping the intermediate exterior angle expression before stating x = 4c.
Equating the exterior angle to the sum of the two remote interior angles with explicit theorem citation.

formal_statement: Two triangles are congruent if two angles and a corresponding side of one triangle are respectively equal to two angles and the corresponding side of the other triangle (AAS).
required_conditions: Two pairs of corresponding angles must be proved equal.
One pair of corresponding sides (in the same relative position) must be equal.

bugs.description: Claiming parallel segments PS and RQ are equal in length (PS = RQ) and citing SAS instead of AAS.
Identifying wrong alternate angle pairs across non-parallel lines.
Stating the two triangles are congruent under AAS without proving the second pair of equal angles (vertically opposite or alternate).
Establishing two equal angle pairs (alternate and vertically opposite) and one equal side (PT = TR) to conclude AAS congruence.

formal_statement: When two parallel straight lines are cut by a transversal, the alternate interior angles formed are equal.
required_conditions: The two lines intersected by the transversal must be given as parallel.
The angles must lie on opposite sides of the transversal between the two parallel lines.

bugs.description: Treating alternate angles as supplementary (summing to 180 degrees) instead of equal.
Citing corresponding angles instead of alternate angles for Z-configured interior angles.
Not stating which pair of lines is parallel when equating alternate angles.
Equating the full alternate angle to the lower transversal angle and solving correctly.

formal_statement: When two parallel straight lines are intersected by a transversal, the co-interior (allied) angles on the same side of the transversal are supplementary (sum to 180 degrees).
required_conditions: The two intersected lines must be parallel.
Both angles must be interior and on the same side of the transversal.

bugs.description: Treating co-interior (allied) angles as equal (110 degrees) instead of supplementary (180 - 110 = 70 degrees).
Applying the alternate angle equality rule to U-shaped co-interior angles.
Writing a = 45 degrees without showing the co-interior angle calculation (180 - 110 = 70 degrees).
Using allied angles summing to 180 degrees to find the corner angle (70 degrees) and subtracting 25 degrees.

name_si: සමද්විපාද ත්‍රිකෝණයක සමාන පාදවලට සම්මුඛ කෝණ
topic: Isosceles Triangle Base Angles with Parallel Lines
formal_statement: In an isosceles triangle, the angles opposite to the equal sides are equal.
required_conditions: Two sides of the triangle must be given or proved equal in length.
The equated angles must be the exact angles opposite to those two equal sides.

bugs.description: Equating the vertex angle between the equal sides to one of the base angles.
Applying the isosceles base angle property to triangle ABC without equal sides.
Stating angle ACB = 70 degrees and b = 70 degrees without citing the angle sum of triangle ABC or equal sides PC = CQ.
Finding angle ACB = 70 degrees via triangle angle sum and equating base angle b = 70 degrees opposite equal sides PC = CQ.
